title: Recording routine: tunes handed over in the studio, publishers paying to be recorded
summary: The band learned the tunes only in the studio; publishers who paid could get Autrey or others to record their songs whether they liked them or not.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: Well when you -- when you got around to broadcasting, or in the recording studio, was everything pretty well routine then? Did -- or did you change things as you went along?

Change things as you went along. We didn't know what tune we were going to record until after we got there, and it was handed to Fats, and Fats reached up, because they was all piled up, five or six tunes, or more, lined up, and he had to pick -- had them stacked, and you take what was next, you know. That's the way they were brought to you, because -- just between the studio and the publishers, they had signed, and they would pass it on to you, because people would come up and buy, well I would like to have Herman Autrey do this tune.
Oh, well I don't know. He's pretty well -- say well, I still want Herman. Well, we'll -- anyway, and they'd write a check. (Laughs). If they wanted to, and pay for it,

and they'd move somebody else over, maybe, if they had to. You know, if they decided to do business. And they'd bring it to the studio, and I had to record it. Whether I liked it or not, which I -- that happened to us so damned many times!
